records.reason: Measure m200 at 1/1 with exactly the loading and DCM volume of measured 3fbf4a3d05e84138e1e2 at 2/1. That row had a historical V2 underprediction of 51.60 mL; together with pure-EA observation 6e07556df6bb6e9df96e, this identifies the solvent-response transition rather than learning only a molecule offset.

Measure m200 at 2/1 and 64.585 mg, halving the load of 3fbf4a3d05e84138e1e2 while keeping loading solvent and volume fixed. The current predictions are nearly loading-invariant. This tests whether the unusually late completion transfers across loads or is specific to the measured loading.

New naphthylethanol m205 at 5/1 tests transfer from naphthylmethanol m206, whose measured row 614873124b33029a924c exposed a large completion failure. The extra methylene and different attachment position make this a useful structural test, with its selected 1/1 partner separating scaffold effects from solvent response.

Pair m205 at 1/1 with its selected 5/1 row at identical 99 mg loading and 400 uL DCM. The predicted endpoints change substantially across this pair; both labels will test whether the response learned from m206 generalizes to this previously unmeasured alcohol scaffold.

m206 in pure EA matches the 100 mg loading of 614873124b33029a924c at 5/1. Its current prediction combines very early onset with V2 near 31 mL. This directly tests the predicted strong-eluent completion behavior in a previously high-error alcohol.

m135 in pure EA matches measured 4d08b9494002d348513d at 1/1 in all other recorded conditions. The model predicts completion near 31 mL versus that measured 15.28 mL, providing a clean test of the predicted rebound in a simpler benzyl alcohol.

m119 in pure EA matches the loading of a775926fce57b3bf9ec1 at 2/1, measured at 20.88/30.18 mL. The predicted much earlier onset but V2 near 36 mL tests whether the completion rebound persists for a methoxyphenethyl alcohol.

m120 at 1/1 matches the 166.95 mg loading of a5f9f0327623c4752e2e at 2/1, where V2 was overpredicted by 12.53 mL. This checks whether the current predicted increase in completion on strengthening the eluent is real and limits transfer of the m200 correction to other donor-plus-acceptor molecules.

m58 in pure EA matches measured 60c07f57327c89c83ae9 at 5/1 and 39963f2ef0f22d86beed at 20/1. Its predicted V2 near 21 mL exceeds the measured 5/1 completion of 11.48 mL. This extends the rebound test from aliphatic alcohols to a sterically substituted phenol.

m177 at 10/1 and 210.9 mg matches the high-load series measured in 76643e968ecc935c745c, 5e276c1730fc0a9deba7 and b514312eda7950cdcf1c. It also contrasts directly with the 140.6 mg measurement ce14dd2481560a984aea. This tests where loading-dependent completion emerges between 5/1 and 20/1.

m177 at 1/1 and 140.6 mg extends the same loading as ce14dd2481560a984aea and 4862e2fb71344ce16021. The model predicts later completion than at 5/1 or 10/1. Measuring this reversal helps distinguish a genuine condition response from interpolation around the irregular nitrobenzophenone observations.

m32 at 5/1 and 50.2 mg makes a direct loading contrast with a4ed6ac3d69b91c56aca at 150.6 mg and a direct solvent contrast with 658deb7d61cd8cd7c4b1 at 20/1. This resolves whether the unexpectedly short completion at low-load 20/1 reflects solvent response, loading, or variability.

This legal candidate repeats the recorded conditions of 658deb7d61cd8cd7c4b1: m32, 20/1, 50.2 mg. That measurement had an 18.39 mL historical V2 overprediction and differs strongly from the higher-load 5/1 observation. One deliberate repeat, paired with the selected low-load 5/1 row, tests reproducibility before interpreting the contrast as a generalizable interaction.

m107 at 1/1 fills the strong-eluent gap between measured pure EA d76d74e2a624a532f9f8 and 2/1 row 143bf510fe2028583763. The 5/1 measurement c6924324ddd95f249df6 reached V2 101.44 mL. This label tests how rapidly the ether-containing acetoacetate response changes; its 109 mg load differs from those 54.5 mg references.

m13 in pure EA preserves the 112.2 mg loading of the measured 2/1, 5/1 and 10/1 series 6573d8f84faaf7ce4a78, a421784c91de559c18e0 and 9e3f598e00375ec93d9b. It anchors the strong-eluent end after earlier retraining produced large overcorrections at intermediate ratios.

m178 at 5/1 uses the same loading as measured 634f21e11a8442494ce3 at 10/1 and 0c5c35afb3a24375c153 at 50/1. Their V2 values differ from 27.45 to 98.73 mL. This adds a lower-retention anchor for the separated diaryl-carbonyl topology and tests whether its response is locally smooth.

m78 at 50/1 preserves the 155.4 mg loading of measured 6000105cb6734cff8146 at 5/1 and b5e6e9a4b5c6f0fa8c0 at 10/1. The model predicts a steep rise to V2 near 66 mL and assigns maximal CW distance. This tests weak-eluent extrapolation for a benzyl-substituted beta-ketoester, rather than selecting it simply for high predicted retention.

m94 at 20/1 and 117.4 mg matches measured 7bd353fc307c5af1997e at 2/1. The model predicts 35.29/68.41 mL, a steep extension beyond existing 2/1 and 5/1 observations. This tests whether the cyclopropyl beta-ketoester follows the solvent sensitivity learned for other acetoacetates.

m129 at 10/1 matches measured cf8ab33c25ad391a584c at 5/1, which eluted at 6.10/17.18 mL despite a substantial historical overprediction. It tests the current predicted sharp increase and enables comparison with the methylthio ketone measurement 92f7fe9d8581717a9949.

m129 at 50/1 pairs with its selected 10/1 row at identical loading. The current prediction reaches 46.86/84.61 mL despite the modest measured 5/1 retention in cf8ab33c25ad391a584c. Two separated condition points distinguish a genuinely steep sulfur-containing aldehyde response from weak-eluent overextrapolation.

m117 at 10/1 probes the predicted acceleration beyond measured c68db037670dea886720 at 5/1, where completion was only 16.98 mL. Alongside pure-EA observation 3fa513c053678904d89c, it tests the solvent dependence of an ortho-hydroxy aromatic aldehyde without assuming all oxygen-rich aromatics need a positive correction.

m186 at 50/1 extends a brominated ortho-hydroxy aldehyde beyond its measured 1/1 rows 47328994eb7953d68919a and cf2b5bd61a8fa92f67a8. Compare with salicylaldehyde 619663c2b3ffb3a6c497 and the selected m117 point, allowing for loading differences, to test substitution-sensitive weak-eluent retention.

m160 at 5/1 and 100 mg extends measured 1/1 behavior in e83... references through the amino-nitrile family. Specifically, a8ae74aecb3b1e85b73c and a160's selected meta-isomer partner provide structural context; the predicted V2 near 70 mL tests whether the sharp amino-ester response observed in d2921349ba8d9cef15a4 transfers to an amino nitrile.

m161 at 5/1 matches the 100 mg loading of measured 0c24b9414856413c9a67 at 1/1, with e12edd0198c0d750ecd5 providing a lower-load 2/1 reference. Pairing it with para-isomer m160 at identical recorded conditions tests positional effects where the model predicts a large completion increase for both.

Dibenzylamine m212 at 5/1 tests a secondary amine, chemically distinct from the pyridines and anilines already measured. Observation ebf38d80f4c5674cf120 at 1/1 provides a strong-eluent anchor, while the current prediction is 20.84/45.56 mL. This expands functional-group-specific solvent learning rather than applying one nitrogen correction.

m66 in pure EA matches the loading of measured 8f5acbec0c511bb1ea89 at 1/1 and 4659b6752f23c0b85f08 at 2/1. Their V2 values are 34.83 and 55.06 mL; the current pure-EA prediction is only 11.63 mL. This tests the strong-eluent boundary of a pyridyl ketone response.

Acetophenone oxime m11 at 5/1 matches the 100 mg loading of pure-EA observation c219b2fe4227fb602c44. It covers a donor/acceptor nitrogen identity with little measured condition coverage and tests a predicted increase from short pure-EA elution to V2 near 30 mL.

Previously unmeasured di-tert-butyl aromatic aldehyde m49 at 50/1 has low similarity to observed molecules. Its bulky hydrophobic substitution tests how the model balances aromatic carbonyl adsorption with steric environment and hydrophobicity, providing a useful boundary for the recurring aldehyde family.

New biphenyl aldehyde m189 at 20/1 tests transfer from the fused aromatic aldehyde measured in 783cf2454912fc14bb80 at the same solvent ratio. The predicted endpoints are similar, but linked versus fused aromatic topology is untested; this label can improve aromatic-size generalization.

New methyl-substituted tetralone m63 at 20/1 tests a cyclic ketone environment against the measured tetralone reference 73a35f890e678b320073 and related ring-expanded ketone b6dc1ec0dbd724128ce3. Differences in solvent ratio are explicit, so this is a transfer test rather than an isolated methyl-substitution effect.

New ethyl chlorobenzoate m84 at 40/1 tests an intermediate weak-eluent ratio in the aromatic ester family. Measured methyl chlorobenzoate 07f6d8c342b66a49bb4e and ethyl fluorobenzoate cd7c523e3df961c83524 supply structural and solvent context. This checks ester-alkyl and halogen transfer without relying only on extreme polar examples.

m155 in pure EA preserves the 169.9 mg loading of measured 98923a8da3524ce0e392 at 1/1 and 279654c9a255466c0dfa at 50/1. The 1/1 completion was unexpectedly late for this acceptor-free arene. This provides a non-donor reference for strong-eluent response and tests whether the current pure-EA decrease is reliable.

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl and ester topology require molecule-dependent solvent-response slopes; a shared oxygen-count correction is insufficient.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched condition labels can teach nonlinear structure-solvent interactions and prevent the large overcorrections seen after acquiring isolated high-retention rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do additional strong- and weak-eluent points support transferable slopes across ether-containing acetoacetates, substituted beta-ketoesters and separated aromatic carbonyls?

hypotheses.content: Nitrobenzophenone shows irregular endpoint-specific loading and solvent contrasts; a smooth loading law has not been established, and variability or unrecorded influences remain possible.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The model remains nearly invariant to loading, but these observations do not justify imposing a monotonic or smooth correction. Targeted contrasts can identify useful interactions and their limits.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 10/1, does high loading retain the short completion seen at 5/1 or move toward the late completion seen at 20/1; does the middle load show a genuine 1/1 reversal?

hypotheses.content: Aromatic carbonyl completion depends on carbonyl identity, substituent placement and oxygen or sulfur environment, with compound-specific weak-eluent slopes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Opposite historical errors within related aromatic families argue for local structure-condition learning rather than a universal late-completion adjustment.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the steep predicted slopes for methylthio and ortho-hydroxy aldehydes supported by additional labels, and do these relationships transfer to bulky or linked-ring aldehydes?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen identity and position govern distinct solvent-response relationships; amino nitriles, amino esters, pyridyl carbonyls, secondary amines and oximes should not share a single retention correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Large condition-dependent errors span chemically different nitrogen groups. Paired isomers and missing strong-eluent anchors can improve transfer across this recurring part of the Row distribution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do amino nitriles show the sharp 2/1-to-5/1 response seen in amino esters, and how do secondary amine, oxime and pyridyl ketone responses differ?

hypotheses.content: Alcohol retention depends on scaffold, donor placement and accompanying acceptors. The new nitrophenethyl alcohol failure warrants a local solvent/loading test rather than a correction for all donor-containing molecules.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The largest recent failure is in a nitro alcohol, while a methoxybenzyl alcohol was substantially overpredicted. Labels must localize the correction and test its structural reach.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: How much of m200's late completion survives stronger eluent or reduced loading, and does naphthylethanol follow the solvent response of naphthylmethanol?

hypotheses.content: The current predictor repeatedly forecasts earlier onset but later completion in pure EA than in intermediate mixtures for donor-containing molecules. This may be a transferable response or a systematic model artifact.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A repeated predicted pattern across several common scaffolds could affect many rows. A small panel of matched pure-EA measurements can distinguish a shared failure from molecule-specific behavior.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do matched alcohol and phenol measurements confirm the predicted pure-EA completion rebound, and how does an acceptor-free arene behave under the same solvent change?

hypotheses.content: The m32 contrast between low-load 20/1 and high-load 5/1 remains ambiguous between a loading-solvent interaction and measurement variability; it does not yet establish an inverted solvent-response curve.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Simple aromatic ketones are common, so fitting an anomalous contrast as a universal solvent effect could damage broad generalization.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the low-load 20/1 result reproduce, and what is the 5/1 response at that same low load?

feedback_interpretation: The latest batch shifts priority toward donor-containing molecules. m200 at 2/1 measured 24.38/69.58 mL, with historical errors of -14.09/-51.60 mL, whereas m120 at 2/1 and m58 at 20/1 had substantial completion overprediction. These outcomes strengthen scaffold-specific modeling and weaken any general donor-retention correction. The m32 weak-eluent completion overprediction motivates a matched low-load point plus one repeat. The m211 overprediction likewise cautions against a universal nitrogen correction. Several ether, ester and neutral references were reasonably accurate, so further generic controls have lower priority. The accurate middle-load m177 10/1 completion supports that local prediction but does not resolve the highly irregular 20/1 and 50/1 loading contrasts; the earlier high confidence in a smooth loading interpretation is reduced. Historical acquisition errors are not treated as current residuals. I also correct two descriptions in the prior memory: 1/1 is an equal PE/EA mixture, not pure EA, and m9 is a linked biphenyl derivative, not a fused aromatic scaffold.
batch_rationale: The batch combines failure repair with experiments that distinguish competing explanations. The m200 solvent/loading contrasts localize the largest recent error. Matched pure-EA donor measurements test a repeated current-model pattern across alcohol and phenol scaffolds, with m155 providing a non-donor reference. The new m205 pair tests structural transfer from the measured naphthylmethanol failure. Oxygenated and sulfur-containing condition points probe steep extrapolations, while amino-nitrile isomers, a secondary amine, an oxime and a pyridyl ketone separate nitrogen environments. A single deliberate m32 repeat evaluates reproducibility before interpreting its unexpected contrast, and the m177 additions probe unresolved loading interactions without assuming smoothness. Four previously unmeasured structures extend chemically relevant aldehyde, cyclic-ketone and ester coverage. Most choices have measured local references, making their labels useful for learning relationships that recur across rows. All 32 choices are distinct eligible candidate IDs, with no pending experiments. Expected benefit is improved retrained V1/V2 prediction across the Row distribution, not improved chromatography of these particular runs; unrecorded influences and imperfect quantiles limit certainty about that benefit.
